evidence.note: Genuine high point: the player climbs at turns 1 and 3, Hall answers with 'Hall: Climb to the top rope.' and both wrestlers end up on the top rope at once - a real positional standoff with both sides at 4 momentum.

The standoff produces a two-way reversal exchange - turn 5 'Hall reverses the hurricanrana - only 2 damage' then turn 6 'Hitman reverses the superplex - only 3 damage, and turns the tables!' - the only stretch with real momentum swing (player 2 -> 5 -> 3).
The trade-off collapses immediately: the player repeats Hurricanrana at a worse 49% and gets the identical outcome as turn 5, with no anti-loop warning to signal the repeat is going stale.
Hall wins the exchange with a 21-damage hurricanrana and the match becomes one-directional - the player's health goes 132 -> 39 while Hall only ever loses 4 HP, all from reversals.
Turns 13, 15, 17, 19 and 21 are all 'Fight to your feet' with exactly one legal option (6 single_choice_turns overall), so the last half of the match contains no decisions at all.
Finish arrives with no buildup - the first cover of the match wins 1-2-3, near_fall_count 0, and the player never reached a Finish option.

Top-rope menu is clear and well differentiated: two 'Big swing' options at 55% noted 'top-rope payoff: high risk, huge crowd pop', a 'Reset / recover' dismount, and a 'Pressure' option at 60% noted 'keep control and build toward a bigger chance'.

Pending groggy is explained as a modifier rather than a position: 'Hitman is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' and it resolves correctly at turn 19 with 'Hitman rises - still groggy from the impact!'

Six of eleven player turns (9, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21) show a single option. The note explains the stake ('stand before they cover you; misses build escape momentum'), but being prompted to choose from one item repeatedly reads as friction.

The anti-loop feedback that this batch added never fires here. The player repeats climb on turns 1 and 3 and Hurricanrana on turns 5 and 7, and no telegraph or stale-loop line appears; the repeated climb even builds momentum (0 -> 2 -> 4), so the menu signals the repeat is fine.

Log freshness gap: turns 5 and 7 emit the byte-identical line 'Hall reverses the hurricanrana - only 2 damage; Hitman whiffs - Hall shrugs it off.', giving no new information about why the second attempt failed.
Probabilities are shown but the moving numbers are unexplained - the tie-up reads 58%-equivalent at 71% on turn 1 and 84% on turn 3 with no indication that momentum is driving the change.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The double-top-rope standoff at turns 4-8 is the most interesting thing in this batch and clearly has unexplored lines (Superplex, Top-rope brawl shot, or dismounting instead of repeating Hurricanrana). Against that, the match is a shutout in which the player lands no offense, spends half its turns on a forced 'Fight to your feet', and loses to the first cover attempted.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 230 choosing 'Top-rope brawl shot' (60%, 'Pressure') at turn 5 instead of the 55% Hurricanrana, and dismounting rather than repeating at turn 7, to test whether the top-rope standoff can be converted into player offense before Hall's turn-8 hurricanrana takes over.

evidence.note: Unexplored content is visible in the menu itself - Superplex, Hurricanrana, Climb down carefully and Top-rope brawl shot were all live and only one was tried, twice.
A 21-damage hurricanrana from the top rope shows the payoff ceiling the player was reaching for, which is a concrete reason to try the position again.
Against rematch: the final five player turns are the same forced get-up attempt with no branching, and the player finishes at 39 HP having never damaged Hall with an intentional move.
The session ends on the first cover with zero near falls, so there is no cliffhanger pulling toward another match.
Position feedback carries the drama: both wrestlers reach TOP_ROPE simultaneously and momentum sits level at 4-4, which reads as a standoff without needing extra text.
Biggest payoff of the match lands with a clear state shift: 'Hall snaps off hurricanrana - Hitman takes 21 damage.' flipping the player to GROUNDED.
Finisher beat is properly tagged - 'Hall snaps off razor's edge - Hitman takes 20 damage.' plus '- FINISHER - the next cover packs extra heat.' - and cashed in at turn 22 as '+12 on the cover!'
finish_sequence pacing metadata is intact (1.0s after 'Referee: 1...', 1.5s after 'Referee: 2...'), but with near_fall_count 0 the count never carries suspense.
Flat repetition undercuts the top-rope spot: the identical reversal line at turns 5 and 7 turns what should be two dramatic misses into one duplicated sentence (log_uniqueness_ratio 0.7857).

The grounded stretch produces low-information text - 'Hitman tries to rise but can't find it - still down and vulnerable to a cover!' appears three times (13, 17, 21) with no escalation as the player's health falls.

top_issues.summary: The anti-loop feedback does not cover the loop that actually happened here. The player repeated Climb (turns 1, 3) and Hurricanrana (turns 5, 7) and no stale/telegraph line appeared in the entire transcript; the repeated climb even gained momentum (0 -> 2 -> 4). The loop tax appears to bite on the tie-up line but not on setup/big-swing repeats.
top_issues.suggested_area: loop tax coverage for climb and top-rope moves

top_issues.summary: 6 of 11 player turns present exactly one option ('Fight to your feet' at 9, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21), so more than half the match asks for input without offering a decision. Turns 13-21 are an unbroken forced-choice stretch.

Shutout with no comeback window - the player never lands an intentional offensive move, Hall's health falls only 132 -> 128 entirely through reversals, and the player never sees a Finish option because Hall is never grounded.
Duplicate log text weakens two separate top-rope misses: turns 5 and 7 emit the byte-identical line 'Hall reverses the hurricanrana - only 2 damage; Hitman whiffs - Hall shrugs it off.'
near_fall_count is 0 and the match's single cover ends it immediately at turn 22, so the pin drama system never engages.
